results.content: # Fed’s Preferred Inflation Meter Unchanged In July—Here’s Why Interest Rates Hikes Are Now More Likely. The Federal Reserve’s favored inflation reading was unchanged in July, according to federal data reported Wednesday, as central bank officials have signaled interest rate hikes unless they see improvements to consumer price increases. Annual inflation was 3.3% in July, according to core personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index data published Wednesday by the Bureau of Economic Analysis, falling above consensus analyst estimates of 3.2% and matching June’s price increases.
